clarifications: What happens if the key is not found in get? Return -1.
Can capacity be zero? No, capacity is always positive.
Are keys unique? Yes, each key is unique.
What if we put a key that already exists? Update its value and mark it as most recently used.
Is the cache size dynamic? No, it remains fixed at the given capacity.
What if we exceed the capacity? Evict the least recently used item.
Are get and put operations expected to be thread-safe? No, assume single-threaded execution.
expectedApproaches: Naive approach using a list with O(n) operations.
HashMap with a doubly linked list for O(1) operations.
solutions: Use a combination of a dictionary and a doubly linked list. The dictionary holds the keys and their corresponding node references in the linked list. The linked list maintains the order of usage, with the head being the most recently used and the tail being the least recently used. This allows both get and put operations to be performed in O(1) time on average.
commonMistakes: Using a single linked list instead of a doubly linked list.
Not updating the order of elements on get operations.
Incorrectly handling the eviction of elements when capacity is exceeded.
Mismanaging pointers in the doubly linked list leading to incorrect ordering.
